answer_1.quote: We propose the THINK-VERBALIZE-SPEAK framework, which decouples reasoning from verbalization to achieve both reasoning accuracy and speech-friendliness...
answer_1.outputs: speech-friendly textual utterances (verbalized summaries) and corresponding spoken audio

answer_2.quote: We adopt the four metrics also used by Cho et al.: (1) Word count (WC)... (2) Flesch Reading Ease (FRE)... (3) Dependency depth (DD)... (4) Nonvocalizable character count (NV)... We also evaluate reasoning accuracy using an LLM-as-a-judge framework.

answer_3.quote: We evaluate the reasoning capabilities of dialogue systems. Each system generates responses to the provided questions, and we assess the correctness of the final outputs using an LLM-as-a-judge framework.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation where Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators rate system responses using a 5-point Likert scale across four criteria: naturalness, conciseness, understandability, and overall quality.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators listen to the spoken response and rate each criterion on a 1-5 Likert scale, providing brief explanations for each rating.
